findings.issue: freezeLegs computes the sibling caps (W - siblingWallet, cardRoom = T - W - siblingRest) from an unlocked read of the order's other returns. The refund lease is per return, not per order, so two returns of the same order can be refunded at the same time and freeze without seeing each other. Two things can then go wrong. (a) The wallet cap's rounding-cent protection is lost, so the direct wallet leg can over-credit by a few cents. This leg goes straight to /internal/wallet/credit and payment-service does not cap it. (b) Both rest legs can be frozen above the real card room. payment-service then rejects the second one with DOMAIN_RULE_VIOLATION on every retry, and because the legs are frozen nothing can clear it, so that return stays PICKED_UP for good. payment-service's refundable-balance check still caps the card leg, so no large over-refund is possible.
findings.fix: In freezeLegs, take a PESSIMISTIC_WRITE lock on the Order row (or bump the Order @Version) before reading the siblings. Concurrent freezes for one order then run one after another. Add a Testcontainers case where two sibling returns are refunded concurrently.

findings.issue: releaseRefundLease sets refund_lease_until = NULL unconditionally. If caller A runs past the 2-minute lease and caller B claims it, A's finally block clears B's lease and a third caller (the admin or ReturnRefundWatch) can enter. Money stays safe because the keys are stable and the attempt bump is conditional, but the mutual exclusion the 409 promises is weaker than documented.
findings.fix: Have claimRefundLease write a per-caller token, or return the lease timestamp it set. Release only WHERE id = :id AND refund_lease_until = :mine.

findings.issue: A missing refundStatus is read as SUCCEEDED, so this fails open on the money path. Only the deploy order written in the runbook guards it. Deploying order-service first, or rolling back only payment-service, would finalize a still-PENDING Razorpay refund (stock released, RETURN_REFUNDED published), and a later FAILED would never be seen.
findings.fix: Treat null as PENDING for PAYMENT_SOURCE routes. The legacy wallet and COD paths settle synchronously, so they can stay SUCCEEDED. Alternatively, fail closed with an explicit contract or version check. At minimum, log a WARN whenever null is mapped.

findings.issue: Pre-V13 PICKED_UP rows where the legacy code already moved money are re-frozen by the new formula. Two cases can pay twice. (1) A legacy COD fallback may already have credited 'return-rest-<id>' directly. The new PAYMENT_WALLET route then credits again under 'return-<id>' (refund-return-<id>) once the COD payment is collectable. (2) The legacy wallet share was round2(R*W/T) with no caps. If the re-frozen w is smaller, the 'return-wallet-<id>' replay returns the old, larger credit while the rest leg also pays the difference. Both need a legacy crash between the money movement and completeRefund, so exposure is small, but nothing detects it.
findings.fix: Before deploy, query PICKED_UP returns that already have 'return-rest-<id>' or 'return-wallet-<id>' wallet_txns and reconcile them by hand. Or, when freezing a legacy row, read the existing wallet txn amount for the key and use that as w, and refuse to route COD through payment-service if 'return-rest-<id>' exists. Add a line on this to the runbook.

findings.issue: There is no SET lock_timeout before the ALTER TABLE. The non-concurrent CREATE INDEX holds a SHARE lock that blocks writes to order_returns while it builds. Both are short at current sizes (the defaults are constants, so there is no table rewrite), but behind a long transaction the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE request queues and stalls all return traffic.
findings.fix: Add SET lock_timeout = '5s' at the top, following the convention the runbook describes for V8. Optionally build the index CONCURRENTLY in a separate non-transactional migration.

summary: No blocker or major findings. Authorization is unchanged and correct: refunds are reachable only through POST /api/admin/returns/{id}/status with hasAnyRole('ADMIN','FINANCE'), there is no new HTTP endpoint, and order-service still reaches payment-service through the existing /internal/payments/orders/{orderId}/refunds and /internal/wallet/credit routes. The new refundStatus field reports only the status of the row under the caller's own idempotency key. The new shippingRefund and refundState fields appear on the return's own response and expose no other user's data. Idempotency keys come from return UUIDs, so they cannot collide across returns, and customers cannot supply them. An exception never moves to a new -r<n> key: only a FAILED reported by payment-service does, and that goes through a conditional rest_leg_attempt bump. Per ADR 0003, FAILED releases the reserved refunded_amount, so retries stay within the payment's refundable balance. ReturnRefundWatch replays the same key under the same lease and JobLock, so it creates no second refund. Finalizing is protected by the PICKED_UP status check and the @Version checks on OrderReturn and Order. COD wallet credit now goes only through payment-service: the COD row is inserted SUCCEEDED and the credit uses key refund-<key> in the same transaction, so a replay is a no-op, and the direct-credit fallback is gone. Shipping can be refunded at most once among live returns. No PII or secrets were added to logs: the RETURN REFUND FAILED line logs only the return and order ids. No dependencies were added. The five minor findings are: sibling legs frozen without an order-level lock (cent-level wallet over-credit, or a permanently stuck card leg); an unconditional lease release; null refundStatus read as SUCCEEDED (fail-open, guarded only by deploy order); legacy pre-V13 PICKED_UP rows that can be paid twice in rare crash cases; and a V13 migration with no lock_timeout.
